**Weekly Audio‑Engineering Practice Plan**  
(Designed for a learner who has been focusing on mixing fundamentals for the past few months)

| Day | Core Focus | Daily Exercise (30‑60 min) | Quick Self‑Test | Milestone for the Week |
|-----|------------|----------------------------|-----------------|------------------------|
| **Monday** | **Gain Staging** | 1️⃣ Pull all channel faders down in your DAW. 2️⃣ Raise each track slowly, listening for clarity and headroom. 3️⃣ Re‑balance the mix using only level moves. | Predict the exact fader level needed to bring a muted track back to a “balanced”‑mix point (check against the actual move). | *Level‑balancing becomes instinctive – you can set a clean gain structure in < 5 min.* |
| **Tuesday** | **EQ** | 1️⃣ Load a multitrack session. 2️⃣ Sweep a narrow boost (±6 dB, Q ≈ 12) across 20 Hz‑20 kHz to locate problematic frequencies. 3️⃣ Replace each boost with a subtle cut (‑2 to ‑4 dB). | Hear a harsh frequency, write down the approximate range, then verify on the spectrum analyzer. | *You can identify and correct the dominant “muddy” or “harsh” band in < 10 s.* |
| **Wednesday** | **Compression** | 1️⃣ Apply an aggressive ratio (8:1) with fast attack/release on a drum track – listen for pumping. 2️⃣ Dial back to a transparent setting (≈2:1, medium attack/release). | Bypass the compressor and tell whether the signal is still “compressed” by feel. | *You can set a transparent compressor that controls dynamics without audible artifacts.* |
| **Thursday** | **Reverb & Space** | 1️⃣ Insert a single reverb on a vocal or snare. 2️⃣ Switch between room, plate, and hall presets, toggling dry/wet to 50 %. | Name the reverb type you just heard and note the perceived distance. | *You can select an appropriate reverb type for any source within 15 s.* |
| **Friday** | **Integrated Mix** | 1️⃣ Take a short (1‑2 min) mix and apply the day‑to‑day tools together (gain → EQ → compression → reverb). 2️⃣ Render a quick “before” version. | After a 5‑minute break, listen and name **one** specific fix you would make. | *Complete a cohesive mini‑mix in ≤ 30 min, demonstrating smooth tool integration.* |
| **Saturday** | **Pure Ear‑Training** | 1️⃣ Play pink‑noise ([[entities/pink_noise]]) and perform an EQ sweep, trying to “flatten” it by ear. 2️⃣ Use a reference track and practice identifying instrument frequency ranges. | Call out the target frequency band before looking at the EQ readout. | *Your ability to match EQ curves by ear improves by ~10 % each week.* |
| **Sunday** | **Critical Listening & Review** | 1️⃣ Choose a professionally mixed song. 2️⃣ Analyze instrument placement, depth, and balance for 15 min. 3️⃣ Compare today’s mini‑mix with the Friday version. | Write a 2‑sentence summary describing how your mix has progressed compared to a month ago. | *Documented progress—noticeable improvement in balance, clarity, and spatial depth.* |

### Weekly Milestones (Beyond Daily Tests)

1. **Speed** – Reduce the total time needed for a full‑mix pass from 60 min (Week 1) to ≤ 30 min (Week 4).  
2. **Accuracy** – Achieve ≥ 80 % correct answers on daily self‑tests (track‑level predictions, frequency guesses, compressor detection, reverb naming).  
3. **Consistency** – Maintain a version‑controlled folder (e.g., “Mix‑Practice/2025‑W01”) and log a brief note after each day; by the end of the month you should see at least three clear *before/after* improvements.  

### How This Fits Existing Knowledge Base

- The day‑by‑day drill layout mirrors the plan outlined in [[summaries/session-04_2025-06-18]] which already recommends 10‑30 min blocks for each mixing fundamental.  
- The overarching structure follows the abstract guideline described in [[concepts/weekly_practice_plan]] and reinforces the ear‑training methodology from [[concepts/ear_training]].  
- Specific tools referenced (DAW, pink‑noise) link to the entity pages [[entities/DAW]] and [[entities/pink_noise]] for quick lookup of software or signal sources.  

---

**Tip for Staying on Track:**  
Create a simple spreadsheet with columns “Date”, “Focus”, “Self‑Test Result”, and “Notes”. Update it after each session; the visual log will make the weekly milestones obvious and help you adjust block lengths if a particular area feels harder than expected.  

Happy mixing! 🎚️
